expected_output.reasoning:
The agent's response correctly diagnoses the issue as a hung Windows Update Agent with a corrupted/bloated scan database (DataStore.edb). It provides the correct fix procedure: stop wuauserv, BITS, cryptsvc, msiserver; force-kill TiWorker if stuck; rename SoftwareDistribution (and catroot2) to force a rebuild of DataStore.edb on next scan; restart services; and trigger a fresh scan with wuauclt/usoclient, then verify CPU settles (confirming scan succeeds). This matches nearly all elements of the expected output: stop wuauserv/BITS, kill hung processes, rename SoftwareDistribution to rebuild DataStore.edb, restart services, confirm scan works.

Minor gaps: it doesn't explicitly mention re-registering WUA DLLs (regsvr32 steps), and doesn't explicitly call out SSU/CBS store corruption as an underlying cause if the issue recurs — though it does address recurrence from a different angle (WSUS approval set, disk space, cleanup). These are relatively minor omissions compared to the core fix which is fully and correctly covered. The response is thorough, technically accurate, and actionable, satisfying the substance of the expected output even though it doesn't mention every single optional item (DLL re-registration, SSU/CBS note).
